column3: NKJV has “the birds of the air,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the birds.”
NKJV has “the parable,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the plural “the parables.”
NKJV has “to know the mystery,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “to you the mystery has been given.”
NKJV has “their sins be forgiven them,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “it be forgiven them.”
NKJV has “in their hearts,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in them.”
Close to the Greek; “fall away” is rendered “stumble.”
NKJV has “this world,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the age.”
NKJV includes “to you who hear,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “more will be added to you.”
